Control settings for the Newton and BFGS optimizers

Source: R/newton_raphson.R
NewtonRaphsonControl.Rd

Tuning parameters shared by Newton-Raphson and BFGS quasi-Newton optimizers inside terradish.

Usage

NewtonRaphsonControl(
  maxit = 100,
  ctol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
  ftol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
  etol = 10 * .Machine$double.eps,
  verbose = FALSE,
  eps = 1e-08,
  del = 1,
  ls.control = HagerZhangControl()
)

Arguments

maxit

Maximum number of Newton or quasi-Newton steps. Increase if the optimizer reports a convergence warning on large or difficult problems.

ctol

Gradient convergence tolerance. Optimization stops when the largest absolute projected gradient is below ctol.

ftol

Objective convergence tolerance. Optimization also stops when the absolute change in the objective is below ftol and the largest absolute projected gradient is below sqrt(ctol).

etol

Eigenvalue threshold used to detect near-singular Hessians. Absolute eigenvalues smaller than etol times the largest absolute Hessian entry are replaced by one when forming the Newton step. Increasing this value regularizes the step at the cost of slower convergence near flat regions.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, report the iteration count, objective value, and gradient norm at each step (emitted with message()). The verbose argument of terradish overrides this field when it is set explicitly.

eps

Box-constraint tolerance. A parameter is considered to be "on the boundary" when it is within eps * abs(par) of the bound. Active-constraint gradient components are zeroed before the step is taken.

del

Typical initial step length for quasi-Newton (BFGS) methods. Used to scale the initial approximate Hessian before any updates are available.

ls.control

Control object for the line search, created by HagerZhangControl (default) or ArmijoControl. ArmijoControl is only valid when optimizer = "bfgs" is passed to terradish.

Value

A named list of class "terradish_newton_raphson_control" holding the settings passed to the optimizer. The elements are the arguments above, validated and stored unchanged: maxit, ctol, ftol, etol, verbose, eps, del, and ls.control (itself a HagerZhangControl or ArmijoControl list). Pass the object to the control argument of terradish; inspect it with str(). The list carries no fitted quantities, so nothing in it needs back-transforming.

Details

The projected gradient sets outward-pointing components at active bounds to zero. A sufficiently small projected gradient gives convergence code 0. A small objective change also gives code 0 if the projected gradient is below sqrt(ctol). Otherwise the optimizer warns that it has stalled and returns code 2. Reaching the iteration limit gives code 1.

For most resistance-surface models the defaults converge reliably. Consider changing them when:

  • The optimizer hits maxit before converging: increase maxit.

  • You want a quick exploratory fit: reduce maxit (for example 5 to 10).

  • The optimizer reports a stall (code 2) or repeated line-search failures: scale the covariates, start closer to zero, or adjust the line search through ls.control.

See also

HagerZhangControl, ArmijoControl, terradish

Other optimizer controls: ArmijoControl(), HagerZhangControl()

Examples

ctrl <- NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 25, verbose = FALSE)
str(ctrl)
#> List of 8
#>  $ maxit     : num 25
#>  $ ctol      : num 1.49e-08
#>  $ etol      : num 2.22e-15
#>  $ ftol      : num 1.49e-08
#>  $ verbose   : logi FALSE
#>  $ eps       : num 1e-08
#>  $ del       : num 1
#>  $ ls.control:List of 10
#>   ..$ delta        : num 0.1
#>   ..$ sigma        : num 0.9
#>   ..$ alphamax     : num Inf
#>   ..$ rho          : num 5
#>   ..$ epsilon      : num 1e-06
#>   ..$ gamma        : num 0.66
#>   ..$ linesearchmax: num 50
#>   ..$ psi3         : num 0.1
#>   ..$ c            : num 1
#>   ..$ verbose      : logi FALSE
#>   ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "terradish_hager_zhang_control" "list"
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "terradish_newton_raphson_control" "list"

# Relaxed tolerances for a quick exploratory run:
ctrl_quick <- NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 10, ctol = 1e-3, ftol = 1e-3)

# \donttest{
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep])

# A tighter, longer-running control than the default
fit <- terradish(Fst ~ forestcover + altitude, data = surface,
                 conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
                 measurement_model = mlpe,
                 control = NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 200, ctol = 1e-8))
coef(fit)
#> forestcover    altitude 
#> -0.09612631 -0.79206795 

# The same fit, reporting each optimizer step. `verbose` is the simple
# switch; it overrides whatever `control` says.
fit_loud <- terradish(Fst ~ forestcover + altitude, data = surface,
                      conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
                      measurement_model = mlpe,
                      control = ctrl_quick, verbose = TRUE)
#> Projected Newton-Raphson with Hager-Zhang line search
#> [1] f(x) = 1.443e+03  |f(x)-fold(x)| = 0.000e+00  max|f'(x)| = 1.291e+02  |f''(x)| = 3.940e+03
#> [2] f(x) = 1.493e+03  |f(x)-fold(x)| = 4.998e+01  max|f'(x)| = 1.530e+01  |f''(x)| = -5.248e+03
#> [3] f(x) = 1.495e+03  |f(x)-fold(x)| = 1.722e+00  max|f'(x)| = 2.609e+00  |f''(x)| = -3.428e+03
#> [4] f(x) = 1.495e+03  |f(x)-fold(x)| = 8.574e-02  max|f'(x)| = 3.715e-01  |f''(x)| = -3.215e+03
#> [5] f(x) = 1.495e+03  |f(x)-fold(x)| = 9.996e-04  max|f'(x)| = 2.617e-03  |f''(x)| = -3.157e+03
#> Solution on interior with `max(abs(gradient))` == 0.00261731205736565 and `diff(f)` == 0.000999619663843987
# }
